title: Trust Floor Remediation
objective: Correct known P0 safety and contract defects in Python without broadening product scope.

stories.title: Enforce protected-name barriers
stories.outcome: Make documented protected names an executable defense at discovery and execution time.
acceptance_criteria: Protected names are rejected even if a future scanner emits them as candidate actions.
Protection is checked again immediately before filesystem mutation.
Claude auto-memory and Codex auth/config/plugins remain non-destructive under every flag.
verification: Unit tests inject protected actions directly into execution.
Adversarial tests cover nested protected paths, symlinks, and aggressive mode.

stories.title: Fingerprint custom provider roots
stories.outcome: Reject destructive use of custom roots that do not credibly match the selected provider layout.
acceptance_criteria: Default roots remain accepted when structurally valid.
Custom roots receive a deterministic provider fingerprint result.
Unknown or low-confidence roots allow inspection but refuse destructive planning/execution.
verification: Fixtures include ordinary project directories containing tmp/log folders.
Negative tests prove no destructive plan is emitted for unrecognized roots.

stories.title: Make aggressive mode retention-safe
stories.outcome: Ensure aggressive expands eligible categories but never silently bypasses age retention.
acceptance_criteria: Every aggressive candidate is subject to the configured retention cutoff unless a future explicitly named all-ages mode exists.
Fresh legacy/cache artifacts remain excluded.
Dry-run and clean select the same artifact set.
verification: Boundary tests at cutoff-1s, cutoff, and cutoff+1s.
Property-style fixture sweep across aggressive categories.

stories.title: Remove ambiguous destructive CLI escalation
stories.outcome: Require the clean subcommand for all destructive behavior and publish stable exit semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Flags without a subcommand never normalize to clean.
Bare cancellai and status remain read-only.
Blocked or partial execution produces a documented non-zero machine-readable exit code distinct from validation failure.
verification: CLI table tests cover every global/common flag without a subcommand.
Automation tests assert exit codes for success, blocked, partial, failure, and invalid usage.

stories.title: Represent incomplete scans and fail closed
stories.outcome: Stop treating unreadable or partially scanned trees as implicitly safe.
acceptance_criteria: Discovery reports completeness for each scanned scope.
PARTIAL and UNKNOWN scan states cannot yield destructive authority.
Status explains unreadable paths without crashing.
verification: Execution tests prove partial inventory cannot produce irreversible actions.

stories.title: Protect concurrent Claude metadata rewrites
stories.outcome: Make history trimming streaming and safe in the presence of active writers.
acceptance_criteria: history.jsonl is streamed to a temporary sibling rather than loaded as a whole.
Shared mutable metadata is never rewritten while Claude is detected active, even with allow-running.
Atomic replace preserves mode and survives malformed lines.
verification: Concurrent mutation simulation verifies new lines are not lost.

stories.title: Fail closed when provider activity is unknown
stories.outcome: Stop treating an unusable process observation as proof that no provider is running.
acceptance_criteria: Process enumeration reports whether it succeeded, separately from which processes it found.
An unusable observation blocks destructive work exactly as a detected running provider does.
Status distinguishes 'no provider running' from 'could not tell'.
verification: Tests simulate ps being absent, failing, timing out, and returning unparsable output.
Execution tests prove no mutation occurs while activity is unknown unless explicitly allowed.

stories.title: P0 regression evidence packet
stories.outcome: Close Trust Floor only with explicit evidence for every P0 defect.
acceptance_criteria: All P0 reproduction cases are converted to permanent regression tests.
No runtime feature beyond P0 remediation is introduced.
Owner-visible Safety Verdict records residual risks and release recommendation.
verification: Independent verifier reruns P0 adversarial scenarios from specification.

stories.title: Report provider layout coverage
stories.outcome: Make the gap between observed provider state and cancellAI-classified state visible instead of silent.
acceptance_criteria: Status classifies every top-level provider entry with a state that matches what cleanup actually does to it, with size.
A container whose contents are selected by age and policy is never classified as deletable in its own right.
Conditional categories state the condition rather than being reported as unconditional.
Unknown entries are reported and never become cleanup candidates.
Machine-readable status output exposes the same coverage classification.
verification: Fixtures include provider directories this build does not classify.
Tests prove an unknown entry cannot enter a destructive plan, including under --aggressive.
Tests prove no container carrying a selective state is ever selected for deletion itself.
